turns.say: I’ll make a silent, 10-second widescreen clip of your Bugatti driving across the Golden Gate Bridge, viewed from the roadside in morning light.

clip.prompt: Use the supplied image as the starting frame and strict visual reference. Create one continuous 10-second, 16:9 silent shot from a stationary roadside camera in natural morning light. PRESERVE Bugatti: its exact recognizable body design and proportions, its light blue and black color placement, and its visible wheels, grille and trim. PRESERVE Golden Gate Bridge: red-orange towers and suspension cables, roadway geometry and pedestrian walkway. Preserve the reference’s visual style and vehicle identity throughout. Establish the bridge setting with blue water and green hills visible beyond the roadside barrier beneath a clear blue sky; do not redesign the car to fit the setting. The Bugatti drives forward along its lane across the bridge at a steady, believable speed, following its initial orientation, with wheels rotating consistently with its travel, tires firmly contacting the road and morning reflections moving naturally across the bodywork. Keep the camera locked off: no pan, tilt, zoom, dolly or cuts. Frame the road so the car remains visible throughout, and hold this unchanged composition on the moving Bugatti for the final two seconds. Maintain coherent vehicle anatomy, perspective, shadows and bridge geometry from first frame to last. Audio off. Negatives: no vehicle morphing, color shifts, warped wheels, sliding tires, floating, sudden acceleration, lane changes, added logos or text, camera shake, transitions or freeze-frame ending.
